pr_title: Fix Steam input "crc" errors, and some other Coverity reports of uninitialized scalar variable
pr_body:
Going through a few reports on https://scan.coverity.com/projects/godotengine-godot?tab=overview

Lots of low hanging fruits there to improve the code quality and find potential bugs.

The input mapping change fixes these issues:
- Fixes #88630
- Fixes #92578

issue_context.title: Parse_mapping error on Steam version only
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.2.2 Steam version only

### System information

Godot v4.2.2.stable - Ubuntu 22.04.3 LTS 22.04 - X11 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1080 Ti (nvidia; 535.171.04) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-7700K CPU @ 4.20GHz (8 Threads)

### Issue description

The Steam version of Godot's gives the following error when pressing the play button to play the game:

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/34660086/86906588-617c-4516-890a-9cc6814c7964)

E 0:00:00:0034   parse_mapping: Unrecognized input string "d95e" in mapping:
03000000010000000100000001000000,input-remapper gamepad,a:b0,b:b1,x:b3,y:b4,back:b10,guide:b12,start:b11,leftstick:b13,rightstick:b14,leftshoulder:b6,rightshoulder:b7,dpup:h0.1,dpdown:h0.4,dpleft:h0.8,dpright:h0.2,leftx:a0,lefty:a1,rightx:a3,righty:a4,lefttrigger:a2,righttrigger:a5,crc:d95e,platform:Linux,
  <C++ Error>    Condition "true" is true. Continuing.
  <C++ Source>   core/input/input.cpp:1494 @ parse_mapping()


The 4.2.2 version in the website does not give the error. My guess is that this is something to do with the Steam controller inputs that Steam automatically injects in games. The error persists even if on Steam you choose "Disable Steam Input" under controller.

### Steps to reproduce

- Open up Godot's Steam version
- Create a Node2D scene
- Press the play button, set the created Node2D scene as main scene
- Error will be shown in the debugger

N/A

review_comments:
Fixes this:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/76894bd1-f248-420d-90c6-e48b60e9fec2)

But this is actually never set anywhere, so the code where it was being used is bogus.

It was added in #80973, CC @ryanabx.

Fixes this type of errors:
![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/0fe2ef91-6b68-4c4d-8904-9782a596e3d7)

CC @rsubtil

Good catch, `expensive` ended up never being set in the code, so this was actually causing undefined behavior.

I can confirm it should be `false` as AFAIK Godot still doesn't support partial/pagination behavior to requesting variables from stack dumps, so there's no point in hinting such behavior to DAP when Godot will already have all that information.

This fixes what I reported here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/73224#discussion_r1587356111

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/4701338/81e6ca45-82c7-4f0b-8b8f-0b92de29ec07)

CC @rsubtil
Yes, it makes sense, I didn't notice that detail when changing the error message to a warning :+1:

I believe this should also fix these issues:
- #88630
- #92578

Although I'm in the blame this is because I'm registered as initial author for 4.x, but this was copy pasted from 3.x GLES2, which is karrofel it looks like.

But fix looks fine to me. :+1:
Removed as the early return makes it dead code.
